concept.subject: Math
concept.title: Equivalent fractions
concept.recall: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number.

questions.prompt: A recipe uses 2/4 of a cup of milk. Write an equivalent fraction with 8 as the denominator.
Explain in one sentence why 3/6 and 1/2 name the same amount.
questions.answer: Rubric: both are one half; multiplying the top and bottom of 1/2 by 3 gives 3/6.

examples.meets: Both are one half because doubling top and bottom keeps the amount.

questions.prompt: Sam ate 6/12 of a pizza. Write the amount he ate as a fraction with a denominator of 2.
Mia says 2/3 and 4/5 are equivalent because she added 2 to the top and the bottom. Explain what went wrong.
questions.answer: Rubric: adding the same number changes the amount; equivalent fractions come from multiplying or dividing the top and bottom by the same number.

mustShow.point: Adding changes the amount; multiplying keeps it
acceptable: times both by the same number

examples.meets: She added 2 instead of multiplying, which changes the amount.
examples.notYet: 4/5 is bigger so it is right.

selfCheck.answer: Yes: each open question has a rubric.
